interrogator_dossier:
# Forensic dossier — Eastroc Beverage (Group) Co., Ltd. (9980.HK / Dongpeng, 东鹏饮料)

**Prepared 7 September 2026.** Sector: consumer staples, non-alcoholic beverages. Signal: deep value / drawdown.
**Price used throughout: HKD 104.60** (Hong Kong H-share line, 9980.HK, quote retrieved 7 September 2026).
The company reports in Chinese yuan; the Hong Kong dollar buys CNY 0.8559 today, so the traded price is
about CNY 89.53 per share.

**A note on sourcing before anything else.** No earnings-call transcript exists for this name in any source
this committee could reach. The paid market-data service carries no transcripts, no news and no analyst
price targets for the Hong Kong line; the primary-source filings service was disconnected; the web-search
budget for this session was already spent, and the finance sites that survive a direct page fetch
(stockanalysis.com, TradingView) carry summary statistics rather than management commentary. What follows is
therefore built almost entirely on the company's own filed income statements, balance sheets and cash-flow
statements, which were pulled independently for both the Hong Kong line (9980.HK) and the Shanghai A-share
line (605499.SS) and cross-checked against each other. Where a claim cannot be sourced, it is not made.
Sections 3 and 5, which depend on hearing management speak, are therefore largely empty, and the credibility
score at the bottom reflects that we could not test management's words at all — not that we found them wanting.

---

## 1. Narrative arc

Eastroc sells Dongpeng Special Drink, the gold-bottled energy drink that has spent five years taking the
Chinese energy-drink market apart, alongside a younger portfolio of electrolyte water, ready-to-drink tea,
coffee and juice. The arc visible in the filings is unusually clean and needs no transcript to read.

From 2021 to 2025 this was a compounding machine: revenue went CNY 6.98bn to 8.51bn to 11.26bn to 15.84bn to
20.88bn, a three-year compound growth rate of roughly 35% a year, with net income tracking it almost exactly
(CNY 1.19bn to 4.42bn). In February 2026 the company added a Hong Kong listing to its existing Shanghai
listing, raising roughly CNY 9.7bn of fresh equity — visible as a CNY 9.76bn financing inflow in the March
2026 quarter and as a near-doubling of shareholders' equity from CNY 9.42bn at the end of 2025 to CNY 20.40bn
three months later.

The arc broke in the first half of 2026, and this is the single most important fact in the file. First-half
revenue was CNY 12.44bn against CNY 10.74bn a year earlier — growth of **+15.9%**, less than half the +31.8%
the company delivered in 2025. Net income was CNY 2.87bn against CNY 2.38bn, **+20.7%**, against +32.7% in
2025. Both figures are confirmed independently on the Shanghai and Hong Kong filings.

So the story has not changed; the rate has. Nothing in the numbers says the franchise is breaking. Everything
in the numbers says the hyper-growth phase that justified the listing price has ended.

---

## 2. Claims versus financials (forensic)

There are no management claims to test. There are, however, several claims embedded in our own screening data
that fail against the filings, and catching them matters more than any quote would have.

| Claim in the screening data | What the filings actually show | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| "Fair value 392.98, margin of safety 281%" | A Buffett-style model extrapolating a 33% earnings growth rate that ended six months ago, and comparing a yuan-denominated output to a Hong Kong dollar price. The two currencies are 17% apart today. | **Unusable.** Discard entirely. |
| "Earnings per share 6.53, up only 2.0% year on year" | Net income rose **+32.7%** in 2025. The share count rose from 520.0m to 676.0m on a 3-for-10 bonus issue, which mechanically flattened per-share earnings. | **Data artifact,** not an earnings stall. |
| "Revenue growth +31.8%" | Correct for the 2025 financial year, but stale. The current run-rate is **+15.9%**. | **Superseded.** |
| "Net debt −7.90bn" | At 30 June 2026: cash CNY 14.47bn plus short-term investments CNY 8.74bn against total debt CNY 6.06bn (including CNY 0.39bn of leases) — **net cash of CNY 17.15bn**, about 21% of the traded market value. | **Understated;** the larger figure is correct. |
| "Insider buy ratio 0.00" | No insider purchases, true. But the 30 June 2026 balance sheet carries **CNY 1.04bn of treasury stock that was not there on 31 March** — the company bought back roughly a billion yuan of its own shares during the second quarter, after the fall. | **Materially incomplete.** |
| "Margin 1.35 standard deviations above historical peak" | Confirmed and important. Gross margin was 44.8% in 2025, is 46.4% over the trailing twelve months, and hit **49.2% in the June 2026 quarter** against 45.7% a year earlier. | **Confirmed — and this is the key risk.** |

Two further observations from the statements that no summary metric captures.

**The working capital is negative and that is a moat reading, not an accounting quirk.** Distributors pay
Eastroc before they receive goods: contract liabilities (customer prepayments) stood at CNY 5.13bn at 30 June
2026, equal to 23% of trailing revenue. Receivables turn in under ten days; payables run 53 days; the cash
conversion cycle is **minus 20.6 days**. The company's customers and suppliers finance its growth. Only
brands with genuine channel power get paid in advance, and it is the same structural feature that makes the
best Chinese consumer franchises worth what they are.

**The margin expansion is real but it is not obviously the company's doing.** Gross margin rose about 2.5
percentage points year on year while volume growth halved. Falling input costs — polyethylene terephthalate
resin for bottles, and sugar — are the most likely explanation, and both are commodity prices rather than
management achievements. Net profit grew faster than revenue (+20.7% against +15.9%) largely because of
this. If input costs turn, the earnings base turns with them.

---

## 3. Tone and confidence trajectory

**Cannot be assessed.** No transcript, investor presentation or management commentary was obtainable for any
quarter. This dimension is genuinely absent from the evidence base and is not being inferred from price
action or from the numbers, which would be a guess dressed as a finding.

---

## 4. Guidance credibility

**Cannot be assessed directly** — no guidance statements were obtainable. One indirect, and quite damning,
observation is available instead.

The published analyst consensus for the 2026 financial year, compiled from 17 analysts for revenue and 8 for
earnings, is revenue of **CNY 28.09bn** (a range of 27.74 to 28.50bn — unusually tight) and net income of
CNY 5.64bn. The company delivered CNY 12.44bn of revenue in the first half. Reaching CNY 28.09bn therefore
requires second-half revenue of CNY 15.65bn against CNY 10.13bn a year earlier — **growth of +54%**, in a
business that just printed +16%.

That is not a forecast anyone would make after seeing the first-half numbers. It is a set of estimates that
has not been updated since the interim report. The screening data's "consensus forward earnings growth
+12.4%" rests on the same stale foundation. **Reliability of the published street numbers: Low.** They are
going to come down.

---

## 5. Analyst pressure points

**Cannot be assessed.** No question-and-answer material was obtainable. What the market is plainly worried
about can be inferred from the tape rather than from analysts: the shares are down about 54% from their
HKD 227.69 high and sit 2% off the 52-week low, and the Shanghai line has fallen almost as far (CNY 241.06 to
CNY 121.98). Whatever the concern is, it is being expressed in both listings and across the wider cohort of
Chinese consumer companies that listed in Hong Kong during 2025 and 2026 — Mixue Group, which listed into the
same enthusiasm, is down from HKD 465.80 to HKD 206.20 over the same window. This looks like a group
de-rating, not a single-company indictment.

---

## 6. Red flags and green flags

🔴 **Red flags**

- **Growth halved, and it happened at exactly the moment the equity was sold.** The Hong Kong listing priced
  in February 2026 on a 2025 record of +32% growth. The first reporting period after the listing came in at
  +16%. Whether or not anyone knew, the sequencing is unflattering and it is the reason the shares are where
  they are.
- **Record-high gross margin carried by falling input costs.** At 49.2% in the June 2026 quarter, the margin
  is at a level the company has never sustained. Our own screen flags it as 1.35 standard deviations above
  the historical peak. A large share of today's profit growth is riding on it.
- **The regime is now working against that margin.** Brent crude rose 9.3% in the week to 4 September 2026
  (USD 88.10 to USD 96.28) on resumed strikes, with the Strait of Hormuz shut. Bottle resin is an oil
  derivative. The single tailwind holding up the earnings beat has just been handed a headwind, with a lag of
  perhaps one to two quarters.
- **We cannot pin down the share count, and the gap is 22%.** The Hong Kong exchange's own float file reports
  895,490,379 shares outstanding as of 7 September 2026, and the three market-data vendors we checked all use
  a number in that region. The company's own 30 June 2026 balance sheet shows share capital of CNY 734.06m at
  one yuan par — roughly 734m shares — corroborated by a weighted-average count of 727.08m for the June
  quarter and by the newly appearing treasury stock. Nothing available today reconciles them. Every per-share
  figure in this file is computed on the **higher, more conservative** count, which marks the business about
  22% dearer than the company's own balance sheet would.
- **Published estimates are stale and must fall.** See section 4.
- **No insider buying.** The company bought stock; the people running it did not.

🟢 **Green flags**

- **Fortress balance sheet.** Net cash of CNY 17.15bn against total debt of CNY 6.06bn, roughly 21% of the
  traded market value. Interest cover above 80 times. Current ratio 1.58.
- **The buyback is real and it was executed into the fall.** CNY 1.04bn of treasury stock appeared on the
  balance sheet between 31 March and 30 June 2026. That is capital allocated against the company's own
  judgement of value, at prices well below the listing price.
- **Profit is still growing faster than revenue.** +20.7% against +15.9% in the first half. Operating
  leverage and mix are intact; this is a deceleration, not a squeeze.
- **Returns remain excellent.** Return on equity 33.7% over the trailing twelve months, and that is *after*
  the dilution from a CNY 9.7bn equity raise that is still sitting in deposits earning very little. Return on
  the capital actually employed in the operating business, once the idle cash is stripped out, is far higher.
- **Cash conversion is genuinely good.** Free cash flow of CNY 4.86bn over the trailing twelve months against
  CNY 4.90bn of net income — the profits are cash.

---

## 7. Hidden signals

Three things sit below the headline numbers.

**The customer prepayment balance is the early-warning system, and we cannot read it yet.** Contract
liabilities went CNY 5.98bn (December 2025) to CNY 4.88bn (March 2026) to CNY 5.13bn (June 2026). Without the
matching June 2025 figure — which was not obtainable — we cannot say whether distributors are pre-ordering
more or less than a year ago. That single line would tell us more about the next two quarters than any
management remark. Anyone underwriting this name should get it.

**The idle cash is quietly flattering and depressing different ratios at once.** The CNY 9.7bn raised in
February sits in deposits and short-term investment products. It adds interest income (CNY 312m over the
trailing twelve months) to reported profit while simultaneously dragging the reported return on invested
capital down from 22.6% to 17.8%. Neither movement says anything about the business. Read the operating
margins instead.

**The Hong Kong line is priced 26.6% below the Shanghai line.** At today's exchange rate the Hong Kong buyer
pays CNY 89.53 for the same earnings a Shanghai buyer pays CNY 121.98 for. That gap is normal for
dual-listed Chinese companies and should not be expected to close — but it does mean a Hong Kong buyer is
paying roughly 13 times earnings for a business the domestic market is paying 18 times for.

---

## 8. Capital-allocation verdict (for the director)

**Trajectory: STABLE.** The earnings base is intact, growing at about 20% and converting fully into cash, on
a balance sheet carrying a fifth of its market value in net cash. What ended was the growth *rate*, not the
business. Calling this deteriorating would confuse a normalisation with a decline; calling it strengthening
would ignore that revenue growth just halved.

**The single thing to weigh before sizing: this is a de-rating from an initial-public-offering price, not a
mispricing from a fundamental base.** The shares have fallen 54% from their high, but they still change hands
at about 16 times trailing earnings on the conservative share count — mid-teens, not distressed. The market
has re-priced a 32%-grower as a 16%-grower and has, on the evidence, got that broadly right. The residual
question is narrow and specific: is 16 times too cheap for a net-cash, negative-working-capital, 34%-return
franchise growing profits at 20%? Probably slightly, but not dramatically — and the answer depends on a
record gross margin that a rising oil price is starting to lean on.

**Economic moat: narrow, and stable.** The moat type is intangible brand plus scale distribution — a
national cold-chain and terminal-outlet network that a challenger cannot rent. The evidence for it is in the
numbers rather than the marketing: a 46% gross margin that is rising, distributors who pay in advance to the
tune of 23% of annual revenue, a negative cash conversion cycle, and a 34% return on equity. The evidence
against calling it wide is equally concrete: this is one category, in one country, against a well-capitalised
incumbent in Red Bull China and against much larger beverage groups now entering the electrolyte-drink
segment the company is relying on for its second act. And the margin expansion that would otherwise argue for
a widening moat is commodity-driven, so it does not count as evidence of growing pricing power.

**Secular threat: manageable.** Chinese functional beverages are a growing category, not a shrinking one. The
sugar-reduction shift is a product-mix problem the company is already addressing with sugar-free and
electrolyte lines, and the rise of instant retail and delivery in China has, if anything, helped single-serve
beverage volumes. None of the eight structural-decline forces this committee tracks fits this business, and
forcing one on it would be an error. The cheapness here is a **fear print with an honest growth reset inside
it** — a re-rating that overshot on the way up and has now mostly, but not entirely, overshot on the way
down. It is not a shrinking base.

Management credibility 3 of 5 · trajectory steady · a narrow but real moat · moat trend steady · structural threat manageable.

bull_thesis:
Eastroc Beverage, better known in China as Dongpeng, is the country's fastest-growing energy-drink brand, and the case for owning the Hong Kong-listed shares at HKD 104.60 is that the market has re-priced a genuinely excellent business as though its growth had stopped, when in fact it merely normalised.

Start with what is not in dispute. Over the trailing twelve months to 30 June 2026 the company earned CNY 4.90bn of net profit on CNY 22.55bn of revenue, a 21.7% net margin, and converted almost all of it into cash (free cash flow of CNY 4.86bn). Return on equity is 33.7%, and that is after February's Hong Kong listing added roughly CNY 9.7bn of fresh equity that is still sitting in bank deposits doing very little. The balance sheet at 30 June 2026 holds CNY 14.47bn of cash plus CNY 8.74bn of short-term investments against CNY 6.06bn of total debt, giving net cash of CNY 17.15bn — on the settled count of 727,076,759 shares that is about a quarter of the traded market value. There is no refinancing risk, no covenant, no maturity wall.

Now the part the tape is ignoring. Growth halved in the first half of 2026 — revenue rose 15.6% to CNY 12.415bn, against 31.8% for the whole of 2025 — but profit rose faster than revenue, up 20.4% to CNY 2.860bn, and gross margin expanded from 45.7% to 49.2% in the June quarter. A company whose demand was genuinely breaking does not widen its margins while it slows. What actually happened is that a 35%-a-year compounder became a mid-teens compounder with better unit economics, which is the normal life cycle of a successful consumer brand, not a warning.

The moat shows up in the working capital rather than in any slogan. Distributors pay Eastroc before they take delivery: customer prepayments stood at CNY 5.13bn at 30 June 2026, equal to 23% of a year's revenue. Receivables turn in under ten days, payables run 53 days, and the cash conversion cycle — the time between paying for goods and being paid for them — is minus 20.6 days. The company's own customers fund its growth. Very few businesses in any market are paid in advance by their channel; the ones that are tend to be the durable franchises.

Management is acting like the stock is cheap. Treasury stock of CNY 1.04bn appears on the 30 June 2026 balance sheet that was not there on 31 March — roughly a billion yuan of shares bought back during the quarter in which the shares fell hardest. The programme was executed at an average of CNY 145.84 an A share, well above today's CNY 121.98, so it is a statement about the company's own value range rather than a mark on today's price; it is still real capital committed rather than a press release.

Finally, the Hong Kong line is the cheap way in. At today's exchange rate of CNY 0.8559 to the Hong Kong dollar, the Hong Kong buyer pays CNY 89.53 per share for earnings the Shanghai buyer pays CNY 121.98 for — a 26.6% discount for identical economics. On the settled 727.1m share count the Hong Kong shares trade on about 13.3 times trailing earnings, 8.1 times enterprise value to earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation, and 9.9 times enterprise value to free cash flow. Nongfu Spring, the closest listed comparison for quality, trades today at roughly 24 times earnings and 15.7 times that same cash-profit measure on materially worse cash conversion.

For this to work, three things must hold. Revenue growth has to stabilise around the mid-teens rather than keep sliding — the 26 October 2026 third-quarter report is the first test. Gross margin has to hold above roughly 46% despite rising oil-linked bottle-resin costs. And the second-act products, chiefly the electrolyte drink, have to keep scaling against much larger entrants. If they do, a business earning 34% on equity with a quarter of its value in cash is worth meaningfully more than 13 times earnings.
bear_thesis:
The bear case is not that Eastroc is a bad business. It is that the recent earnings are flattered by something outside management's control, that the numbers the market is anchored to have not yet been cut, and that the only visible corporate bid was struck well above today's price.

Begin with the cheapness, because a large part of the advertised discount evaporates on inspection. Our own screening record shows a fair value of 392.98 and a 281% margin of safety. That figure extrapolates a 33%-a-year earnings growth rate that ended six months ago and, worse, compares a yuan-denominated output to a Hong Kong dollar price when the two currencies are 17% apart. It is arithmetically meaningless and must be discarded. The same record's 'earnings per share up only 2.0%' is the mirror-image error in the other direction — an artefact of the 3-for-10 bonus issue that took the share count from 520.0m to 676.0m, not an earnings stall. Once both errors are cleared and the denominator is settled at 727,076,759 shares, the stock trades on roughly 13 times trailing earnings and 3.3 times book value. That is a fair multiple for a mid-teens grower, not a distressed one — the bear case does not need the shares to be expensive, only to be priced for margins and volumes that may not arrive. Our own valuation stack agrees it is split: of five independent methods, two say the shares are overvalued (the earnings-power method by 84%, the owner-earnings method by 22%).

Second, the profit growth is being carried by a commodity windfall. Gross margin reached 49.2% in the June 2026 quarter against 45.7% a year earlier, a level the company has never sustained and which our screen flags as 1.35 standard deviations above the historical peak. Bottle resin is an oil derivative, and Brent crude rose 9.3% in the week to 4 September 2026 (USD 88.10 to USD 96.28) with the Strait of Hormuz shut. Strip the margin back to the 2025 level of 44.8% and roughly CNY 800m of annualised gross profit disappears — enough to turn 20% profit growth into low single digits on unchanged volumes. The one thing holding the earnings line up has just been handed a headwind.

Third, the published estimates are stale and have to come down. The consensus for the 2026 financial year, from 17 analysts, is revenue of CNY 28.09bn. The company delivered CNY 12.415bn in the first half. Getting to CNY 28.09bn requires roughly 55% second-half growth in a business that just printed 15.6%. Nobody would forecast that having seen the interim numbers, which means the estimates simply have not been revised. When they are, the stock will look more expensive on forward earnings than it does today, and downgrade cycles in Chinese consumer names have a way of running longer than the fundamentals warrant.

Fourth, the fall is a de-rating, not a dislocation. The shares came to Hong Kong in February 2026, ran to HKD 227.69, and have given it all back plus more. The Shanghai line fell almost as far, from CNY 241.06 to CNY 121.98, and Mixue — the other hot Chinese consumer listing of the same window — is down from HKD 465.80 to HKD 206.20. This is an entire cohort unwinding an initial-public-offering bubble. Buying the sixth month of a cohort de-rating on the grounds that the chart looks washed out has no edge in it, and a stock 2% off its 52-week low with no dated event to force a re-rate can spend a long time going nowhere.

Fifth, the one corporate bid in the file is not a valuation signal. The CNY 1.04bn repurchase that the bull case reads as management calling its own stock cheap was 7,122,551 A shares for CNY 1,038,719,867.57, an average of CNY 145.84, per the 2 September 2026 buyback progress announcement. That is roughly 20% above the CNY 121.98 the A shares fetch today. The company was buying, but it was buying higher; the programme says nothing about today's price being management's value point, and capital already spent above the current mark is not support beneath the shares.

What would confirm the bear case: third-quarter revenue growth on 26 October 2026 below roughly 12%, a gross margin back under 46%, or a fall in customer prepayments (CNY 5.13bn at 30 June) against the prior year, which would say distributors are destocking. Any of those and the earnings base itself, not just the multiple, is in question.
consensus_delta:
The usual question for a beaten-down value name is whether the market is pricing terminal decline into a business with stable earnings power. Here the answer is more interesting, and it cuts against us as much as for us: **the price has already worked out what the published estimates have not.**

The specific street assumption that is factually wrong is the 2026 revenue consensus. Seventeen analysts carry an average of CNY 28.09bn in a strikingly tight band of CNY 27.74bn to CNY 28.50bn. Eastroc delivered CNY 12.44bn of revenue in the first half of 2026. Reaching the consensus therefore requires second-half revenue of CNY 15.65bn against CNY 10.13bn a year earlier — growth of 54% — from a company that just grew 15.9%. No analyst who had read the interim report would publish that number. The estimates have simply not been refreshed since the results, and our own screening record's 'consensus forward earnings growth +12.4%' inherits the same stale base. The consensus earnings figure of CNY 5.64bn is less absurd but still demands 36% second-half profit growth against 20.7% delivered in the first half.

So where we disagree with the market is not that we are more bullish than the street — we are more bearish than the printed numbers, and roughly level with the price. The stock at HKD 104.60 already reflects a mid-teens grower; the estimates still describe a 35% grower. When those estimates are cut, the headlines will read as a downgrade cycle even though the price has known for months. That is the trap in this name: the obvious contrarian read — 'everyone hates it, the numbers are fine' — has the causality backwards.

There is one place where we genuinely differ from the tape, and it is narrower than the drawdown suggests. The market is treating the deceleration as a quality event. It is not. Profit grew faster than revenue (+20.7% against +15.9%), gross margin widened from 45.7% to 49.2% in the June quarter, return on equity is 33.7% after a large dilutive equity raise, distributors still pay in advance to the tune of CNY 5.13bn, and the cash conversion cycle is minus 20.6 days. Those are not the fingerprints of a franchise losing grip. A business with those characteristics growing profit at 20% is worth more than 16 times earnings — but 'more' here means roughly 19 times, not the 40-plus times the shares carried in the spring. The mispricing is real and it is about 17% wide. It is not the 281% our own screen advertised, and the gap between those two numbers is the whole reason this record exists.
forcing_function:
There is no hard date, no proxy window and no corporate event that contractually forces a re-rating here, and it would be dishonest to manufacture one. What exists is a sequence of scheduled checkpoints at which the market can change its mind.

**26 October 2026 — the third-quarter report** (date listed on TradingView's company page, retrieved 7 September 2026). This is the moment that matters most in the next six months. It answers the only question that decides this name: did revenue growth stabilise in the mid-teens, or did it keep sliding? And did gross margin hold above 46% as bottle-resin costs began to rise? A print showing 15%-plus revenue growth with the margin intact converts this from a watchlist name into a buy, because it would confirm that a 34%-return, net-cash franchise is being valued as a cyclical. A print below 12% growth, or a margin under 46%, and the earnings base itself is in question rather than just the multiple.

**The customer prepayment line in that same report.** Contract liabilities were CNY 5.13bn at 30 June 2026. Set against the prior-year figure — which we could not obtain and which anyone underwriting this should insist on — it is the single best forward indicator in the accounts, because distributors pre-order before shipments show up in revenue.

**A continued or enlarged buyback.** The CNY 1.04bn repurchased in the June quarter is the company's own statement about value. Extending it materially at these prices would be the clearest signal management believes the fall has overshot.

**Estimate resets.** The published 2026 consensus needs to fall roughly 15% to become arithmetically possible. Paradoxically, that cut landing is a positive event, not a negative one: it removes the last reason for a marginal buyer to stay away, and it is the point at which the forward multiple stops being a fiction.
valley_of_death:
There is no cash-burn hump and no maturity wall here — with CNY 17.15bn of net cash, interest cover above 80 times and CNY 4.86bn of annual free cash flow, the company cannot be forced into anything. The risky window over the next three to nine months is entirely about earnings quality and the estimate cycle.

**The margin unwind is the live danger, and its clock has already started.** The June 2026 quarter's 49.2% gross margin is the highest the company has ever posted and our own screen flags it as 1.35 standard deviations above the historical peak. The most plausible driver is falling input costs — polyethylene terephthalate resin for the bottles and sugar. Brent crude rose 9.3% in the week to 4 September 2026, from USD 88.10 to USD 96.28, on resumed strikes with the Strait of Hormuz shut 189 days. Resin prices follow crude with a lag of roughly one to two quarters, which puts the cost increase into the December 2026 and March 2027 reporting periods. Reverting the margin to 2025's 44.8% removes roughly CNY 800m of annualised gross profit — enough to take profit growth from 20% to low single digits on unchanged volumes. This is the one place where the current market regime has a genuinely live transmission channel into this name, and it points the wrong way.

**The estimate cut is close to certain and has not happened yet.** Analysts are still carrying 54% second-half revenue growth. Those numbers will be marked down, most likely around the third-quarter report on 26 October 2026. Headline downgrade risk is therefore concentrated in the next seven weeks, and downgrade cycles in Chinese consumer names typically run in three or four waves rather than one.

**The cohort de-rating may not be finished.** Mixue is down 56% from its high, Nongfu is down 26%, and both Eastroc listings are down roughly half. Nothing in the tape says the unwind of the 2025-26 Chinese consumer listing boom has found its floor, and a stock sitting 2% off its 52-week low has no technical support beneath it.

**The measurement risk we cannot resolve.** The 22% discrepancy between the exchange's reported share count of 895.5m and the company's balance-sheet implied 734m is not itself a business risk, but it means any position taken today is sized against a denominator we have not verified. That is a reason to wait for clarity rather than to buy through it.
positioning_washout:
This is not a yield-driven shareholder base and there is no dividend cut in prospect, so the classic mechanical-liquidation setup does not apply. The dividend is roughly 2.1% of the price on the trailing payout of CNY 1.88 a share; note that two widely used data providers quote 5.5% and 6.0% for this name, both of which appear to annualise an older, higher payout against the new, much lower price. The yield here is not a support and should not be treated as one.

The forced-selling pressure that matters is the unwinding of an initial-public-offering shareholder register. The Hong Kong shares listed on 3 February 2026, ran to HKD 227.69, and are now at HKD 104.60 — roughly 45% below where the offering priced. Every investor who bought the deal or bought into the first-quarter enthusiasm is deeply underwater, and the standard six-month lock-up on such an offering would have expired around early August 2026. We could not retrieve the offering documents to confirm the specific lock-up terms, so this is not asserted as fact; but the shape of the decline — steady, persistent, into a rising volume of shares available to trade, with the low printed only days ago — is consistent with supply rather than with a single shock.

Working the other way, the company itself has been a buyer: roughly CNY 1.04bn of stock repurchased during the June 2026 quarter. That is the only large, price-insensitive bid visible in the file, and it is a real one.

The honest read is that the washout is well advanced but probably not complete. The shares sit 2% above their 52-week low and 29% below their 200-day average, which is the profile of a market still finding sellers rather than one that has run out of them. A capitulation low, if it comes, would most likely be printed around the third-quarter report when the estimate cuts land.
moderator_conclusion:
**Buy it here.** The first pass called this a good business at a fair price and told the committee to wait for roughly HKD 90. That instruction rested on a denominator that has since been settled against the company's own filings, and with the correct one the same schedule produces a different answer.

The quality was never the argument. Eastroc earns a 33.7% return on equity, converts essentially all of its profit into cash, carries CNY 17.15bn of net cash — about a quarter of its market value on the settled count — and is paid in advance by its distributors to the tune of 23% of a year's revenue. Its cash conversion cycle is minus 20.6 days. Those are the marks of a genuine consumer franchise, and they are why the moat reads as narrow but real and stable rather than eroding: the margins are widening, not contracting, and no structural force this committee tracks threatens the terminal value of Chinese functional beverages.

The price is no longer the problem. On 727,076,759 shares outstanding the shares trade at about 13.3 times trailing earnings and 3.3 times book, roughly 10 times once net cash is stripped out. Base fair value is HKD 150 against a HKD 104.60 quote — a 30.3% discount, which clears this book's 20% entry-discount floor in the current GOLDILOCKS quadrant rather than missing it. Against an adverse case of HKD 82 the trade-off is 43% up for 22% down, a reward to risk of 2.01 where the first pass computed 0.46. There is still no structural floor: net cash is worth about HKD 27.5 a share and there is no deal, tender or fixed distribution to catch the price, so the downside remains bounded by the multiple.

Two of the three things that previously held the conviction at neutral survive; the third does not. The growth reset is real — 15.6% revenue growth in the first half of 2026 against 31.8% for 2025, confirmed on both listings — and the profit growth that survives is riding on a record 49.2% gross margin most plausibly caused by falling oil-linked input costs, with Brent up 9.3% in the week to 4 September 2026 and the Strait of Hormuz shut. That is the one place where the current regime reaches directly into this business, and it points against us; it is why the 18-month horizon and a mid-teens, not a mid-thirties, growth assumption are carried. The third holdback, the unresolved share count, is gone: 734,199,310 issued less 7,122,551 in treasury gives 727,076,759, tied to the interim distribution total and the Q2 weighted-average count. The record's own conservatism has been paid back rather than punished.

One bear-side fact travels with the correction and is worth stating plainly. The CNY 1.04bn buyback was executed at an average of CNY 145.84 an A share against CNY 121.98 today, so it is evidence of management's value range, not confirmation that today's price is their entry. It should not be read as a bid beneath the stock.

On the catalyst, we apply no penalty and no credit. The listing has happened and its re-rating has fully reversed; the buyback has happened; what remains is a soft catalyst with no fixed date and no contractual payout. In this book that is a description, not a mark against the name — but it is also why this is a conviction 4 and not higher: the discount is wide and the balance sheet is unarguable, yet nothing on the calendar forces the re-rating. The **26 October 2026 third-quarter report** remains the test that either accelerates it or breaks it: revenue growth holding at 15% or better with gross margin above 46% despite rising resin costs, and customer prepayments up year on year, and the case strengthens; a print below 12% growth or a margin under 46% and the earnings base, not just the multiple, is in question. Verdict held at B — the setup is a wide discount on a quality compounder without a dated forcing event, which is exactly what a B describes — with conviction lifted from 3 to 4 because the arithmetic that argued for waiting no longer does.

interrogator_dossier:
# Forensic dossier — Eastroc Beverage (Group) Co., Ltd. (9980.HK / Dongpeng, 东鹏饮料)

**Prepared 7 September 2026.** Sector: consumer staples, non-alcoholic beverages. Signal: deep value / drawdown.
**Price used throughout: HKD 104.60** (Hong Kong H-share line, 9980.HK, quote retrieved 7 September 2026).
The company reports in Chinese yuan; the Hong Kong dollar buys CNY 0.8559 today, so the traded price is
about CNY 89.53 per share.

**A note on sourcing before anything else.** No earnings-call transcript exists for this name in any source
this committee could reach. The paid market-data service carries no transcripts, no news and no analyst
price targets for the Hong Kong line; the primary-source filings service was disconnected; the web-search
budget for this session was already spent, and the finance sites that survive a direct page fetch
(stockanalysis.com, TradingView) carry summary statistics rather than management commentary. What follows is
therefore built almost entirely on the company's own filed income statements, balance sheets and cash-flow
statements, which were pulled independently for both the Hong Kong line (9980.HK) and the Shanghai A-share
line (605499.SS) and cross-checked against each other. Where a claim cannot be sourced, it is not made.
Sections 3 and 5, which depend on hearing management speak, are therefore largely empty, and the credibility
score at the bottom reflects that we could not test management's words at all — not that we found them wanting.

---

## 1. Narrative arc

Eastroc sells Dongpeng Special Drink, the gold-bottled energy drink that has spent five years taking the
Chinese energy-drink market apart, alongside a younger portfolio of electrolyte water, ready-to-drink tea,
coffee and juice. The arc visible in the filings is unusually clean and needs no transcript to read.

From 2021 to 2025 this was a compounding machine: revenue went CNY 6.98bn to 8.51bn to 11.26bn to 15.84bn to
20.88bn, a three-year compound growth rate of roughly 35% a year, with net income tracking it almost exactly
(CNY 1.19bn to 4.42bn). In February 2026 the company added a Hong Kong listing to its existing Shanghai
listing, raising roughly CNY 9.7bn of fresh equity — visible as a CNY 9.76bn financing inflow in the March
2026 quarter and as a near-doubling of shareholders' equity from CNY 9.42bn at the end of 2025 to CNY 20.40bn
three months later.

The arc broke in the first half of 2026, and this is the single most important fact in the file. First-half
revenue was CNY 12.44bn against CNY 10.74bn a year earlier — growth of **+15.9%**, less than half the +31.8%
the company delivered in 2025. Net income was CNY 2.87bn against CNY 2.38bn, **+20.7%**, against +32.7% in
2025. Both figures are confirmed independently on the Shanghai and Hong Kong filings.

So the story has not changed; the rate has. Nothing in the numbers says the franchise is breaking. Everything
in the numbers says the hyper-growth phase that justified the listing price has ended.

---

## 2. Claims versus financials (forensic)

There are no management claims to test. There are, however, several claims embedded in our own screening data
that fail against the filings, and catching them matters more than any quote would have.

| Claim in the screening data | What the filings actually show | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| "Fair value 392.98, margin of safety 281%" | A Buffett-style model extrapolating a 33% earnings growth rate that ended six months ago, and comparing a yuan-denominated output to a Hong Kong dollar price. The two currencies are 17% apart today. | **Unusable.** Discard entirely. |
| "Earnings per share 6.53, up only 2.0% year on year" | Net income rose **+32.7%** in 2025. The share count rose from 520.0m to 676.0m on a 3-for-10 bonus issue, which mechanically flattened per-share earnings. | **Data artifact,** not an earnings stall. |
| "Revenue growth +31.8%" | Correct for the 2025 financial year, but stale. The current run-rate is **+15.9%**. | **Superseded.** |

Two further observations from the statements that no summary metric captures.

**The working capital is negative and that is a moat reading, not an accounting quirk.** Distributors pay
Eastroc before they receive goods: contract liabilities (customer prepayments) stood at CNY 5.13bn at 30 June
2026, equal to 23% of trailing revenue. Receivables turn in under ten days; payables run 53 days; the cash
conversion cycle is **minus 20.6 days**. The company's customers and suppliers finance its growth. Only
brands with genuine channel power get paid in advance, and it is the same structural feature that makes the
best Chinese consumer franchises worth what they are.

**The margin expansion is real but it is not obviously the company's doing.** Gross margin rose about 2.5
percentage points year on year while volume growth halved. Falling input costs — polyethylene terephthalate
resin for bottles, and sugar — are the most likely explanation, and both are commodity prices rather than
management achievements. Net profit grew faster than revenue (+20.7% against +15.9%) largely because of
this. If input costs turn, the earnings base turns with them.

---

## 3. Tone and confidence trajectory

**Cannot be assessed.** No transcript, investor presentation or management commentary was obtainable for any
quarter. This dimension is genuinely absent from the evidence base and is not being inferred from price
action or from the numbers, which would be a guess dressed as a finding.

---

## 4. Guidance credibility

**Cannot be assessed directly** — no guidance statements were obtainable. One indirect, and quite damning,
observation is available instead.

The published analyst consensus for the 2026 financial year, compiled from 17 analysts for revenue and 8 for
earnings, is revenue of **CNY 28.09bn** (a range of 27.74 to 28.50bn — unusually tight) and net income of
CNY 5.64bn. The company delivered CNY 12.44bn of revenue in the first half. Reaching CNY 28.09bn therefore
requires second-half revenue of CNY 15.65bn against CNY 10.13bn a year earlier — **growth of +54%**, in a
business that just printed +16%.

That is not a forecast anyone would make after seeing the first-half numbers. It is a set of estimates that
has not been updated since the interim report. The screening data's "consensus forward earnings growth
+12.4%" rests on the same stale foundation. **Reliability of the published street numbers: Low.** They are
going to come down.

---

## 5. Analyst pressure points

**Cannot be assessed.** No question-and-answer material was obtainable. What the market is plainly worried
about can be inferred from the tape rather than from analysts: the shares are down about 54% from their
HKD 227.69 high and sit 2% off the 52-week low, and the Shanghai line has fallen almost as far (CNY 241.06 to
CNY 121.98). Whatever the concern is, it is being expressed in both listings and across the wider cohort of
Chinese consumer companies that listed in Hong Kong during 2025 and 2026 — Mixue Group, which listed into the
same enthusiasm, is down from HKD 465.80 to HKD 206.20 over the same window. This looks like a group
de-rating, not a single-company indictment.

---

## 6. Red flags and green flags

🔴 **Red flags**

- **Growth halved, and it happened at exactly the moment the equity was sold.** The Hong Kong listing priced
  in February 2026 on a 2025 record of +32% growth. The first reporting period after the listing came in at
  +16%. Whether or not anyone knew, the sequencing is unflattering and it is the reason the shares are where
  they are.
- **Record-high gross margin carried by falling input costs.** At 49.2% in the June 2026 quarter, the margin
  is at a level the company has never sustained. Our own screen flags it as 1.35 standard deviations above
  the historical peak. A large share of today's profit growth is riding on it.
- **The regime is now working against that margin.** Brent crude rose 9.3% in the week to 4 September 2026
  (USD 88.10 to USD 96.28) on resumed strikes, with the Strait of Hormuz shut. Bottle resin is an oil
  derivative. The single tailwind holding up the earnings beat has just been handed a headwind, with a lag of
  perhaps one to two quarters.
- **We cannot pin down the share count, and the gap is 22%.** The Hong Kong exchange's own float file reports
  895,490,379 shares outstanding as of 7 September 2026, and the three market-data vendors we checked all use
  a number in that region. The company's own 30 June 2026 balance sheet shows share capital of CNY 734.06m at
  one yuan par — roughly 734m shares — corroborated by a weighted-average count of 727.08m for the June
  quarter and by the newly appearing treasury stock. Nothing available today reconciles them. Every per-share
  figure in this file is computed on the **higher, more conservative** count, which marks the business about
  22% dearer than the company's own balance sheet would.
- **Published estimates are stale and must fall.** See section 4.
- **No insider buying.** The company bought stock; the people running it did not.

🟢 **Green flags**

- **Fortress balance sheet.** Net cash of CNY 17.15bn against total debt of CNY 6.06bn, roughly 21% of the
  traded market value. Interest cover above 80 times. Current ratio 1.58.
- **The buyback is real and it was executed into the fall.** CNY 1.04bn of treasury stock appeared on the
  balance sheet between 31 March and 30 June 2026. That is capital allocated against the company's own
  judgement of value, at prices well below the listing price.
- **Profit is still growing faster than revenue.** +20.7% against +15.9% in the first half. Operating
  leverage and mix are intact; this is a deceleration, not a squeeze.
- **Returns remain excellent.** Return on equity 33.7% over the trailing twelve months, and that is *after*
  the dilution from a CNY 9.7bn equity raise that is still sitting in deposits earning very little. Return on
  the capital actually employed in the operating business, once the idle cash is stripped out, is far higher.
- **Cash conversion is genuinely good.** Free cash flow of CNY 4.86bn over the trailing twelve months against
  CNY 4.90bn of net income — the profits are cash.

---

## 7. Hidden signals

Three things sit below the headline numbers.

**The customer prepayment balance is the early-warning system, and we cannot read it yet.** Contract
liabilities went CNY 5.98bn (December 2025) to CNY 4.88bn (March 2026) to CNY 5.13bn (June 2026). Without the
matching June 2025 figure — which was not obtainable — we cannot say whether distributors are pre-ordering
more or less than a year ago. That single line would tell us more about the next two quarters than any
management remark. Anyone underwriting this name should get it.

**The idle cash is quietly flattering and depressing different ratios at once.** The CNY 9.7bn raised in
February sits in deposits and short-term investment products. It adds interest income (CNY 312m over the
trailing twelve months) to reported profit while simultaneously dragging the reported return on invested
capital down from 22.6% to 17.8%. Neither movement says anything about the business. Read the operating
margins instead.

**The Hong Kong line is priced 26.6% below the Shanghai line.** At today's exchange rate the Hong Kong buyer
pays CNY 89.53 for the same earnings a Shanghai buyer pays CNY 121.98 for. That gap is normal for
dual-listed Chinese companies and should not be expected to close — but it does mean a Hong Kong buyer is
paying roughly 13 times earnings for a business the domestic market is paying 18 times for.

---

## 8. Capital-allocation verdict (for the director)

**Trajectory: STABLE.** The earnings base is intact, growing at about 20% and converting fully into cash, on
a balance sheet carrying a fifth of its market value in net cash. What ended was the growth *rate*, not the
business. Calling this deteriorating would confuse a normalisation with a decline; calling it strengthening
would ignore that revenue growth just halved.

**The single thing to weigh before sizing: this is a de-rating from an initial-public-offering price, not a
mispricing from a fundamental base.** The shares have fallen 54% from their high, but they still change hands
at about 16 times trailing earnings on the conservative share count — mid-teens, not distressed. The market
has re-priced a 32%-grower as a 16%-grower and has, on the evidence, got that broadly right. The residual
question is narrow and specific: is 16 times too cheap for a net-cash, negative-working-capital, 34%-return
franchise growing profits at 20%? Probably slightly, but not dramatically — and the answer depends on a
record gross margin that a rising oil price is starting to lean on.

**Economic moat: narrow, and stable.** The moat type is intangible brand plus scale distribution — a
national cold-chain and terminal-outlet network that a challenger cannot rent. The evidence for it is in the
numbers rather than the marketing: a 46% gross margin that is rising, distributors who pay in advance to the
tune of 23% of annual revenue, a negative cash conversion cycle, and a 34% return on equity. The evidence
against calling it wide is equally concrete: this is one category, in one country, against a well-capitalised
incumbent in Red Bull China and against much larger beverage groups now entering the electrolyte-drink
segment the company is relying on for its second act. And the margin expansion that would otherwise argue for
a widening moat is commodity-driven, so it does not count as evidence of growing pricing power.

**Secular threat: manageable.** Chinese functional beverages are a growing category, not a shrinking one. The
sugar-reduction shift is a product-mix problem the company is already addressing with sugar-free and
electrolyte lines, and the rise of instant retail and delivery in China has, if anything, helped single-serve
beverage volumes. None of the eight structural-decline forces this committee tracks fits this business, and
forcing one on it would be an error. The cheapness here is a **fear print with an honest growth reset inside
it** — a re-rating that overshot on the way up and has now mostly, but not entirely, overshot on the way
down. It is not a shrinking base.

Management credibility 3 of 5 · trajectory steady · a narrow but real moat · moat trend steady · structural threat manageable.

bull_thesis:
Eastroc Beverage, better known in China as Dongpeng, is the country's fastest-growing energy-drink brand, and the case for owning the Hong Kong-listed shares at HKD 104.60 is that the market has re-priced a genuinely excellent business as though its growth had stopped, when in fact it merely normalised.

Start with what is not in dispute. Over the trailing twelve months to 30 June 2026 the company earned CNY 4.90bn of net profit on CNY 22.55bn of revenue, a 21.7% net margin, and converted almost all of it into cash (free cash flow of CNY 4.86bn). Return on equity is 33.7%, and that is after February's Hong Kong listing added roughly CNY 9.7bn of fresh equity that is still sitting in bank deposits doing very little. The balance sheet at 30 June 2026 holds CNY 14.47bn of cash plus CNY 8.74bn of short-term investments against CNY 6.06bn of total debt, giving net cash of CNY 17.15bn — on the settled count of 727,076,759 shares that is about a quarter of the traded market value. There is no refinancing risk, no covenant, no maturity wall.

Now the part the tape is ignoring. Growth halved in the first half of 2026 — revenue rose 15.6% to CNY 12.415bn, against 31.8% for the whole of 2025 — but profit rose faster than revenue, up 20.4% to CNY 2.860bn, and gross margin expanded from 45.7% to 49.2% in the June quarter. A company whose demand was genuinely breaking does not widen its margins while it slows. What actually happened is that a 35%-a-year compounder became a mid-teens compounder with better unit economics, which is the normal life cycle of a successful consumer brand, not a warning.

The moat shows up in the working capital rather than in any slogan. Distributors pay Eastroc before they take delivery: customer prepayments stood at CNY 5.13bn at 30 June 2026, equal to 23% of a year's revenue. Receivables turn in under ten days, payables run 53 days, and the cash conversion cycle — the time between paying for goods and being paid for them — is minus 20.6 days. The company's own customers fund its growth. Very few businesses in any market are paid in advance by their channel; the ones that are tend to be the durable franchises.

Management is acting like the stock is cheap. Treasury stock of CNY 1.04bn appears on the 30 June 2026 balance sheet that was not there on 31 March — roughly a billion yuan of shares bought back during the quarter in which the shares fell hardest. The programme was executed at an average of CNY 145.84 an A share, well above today's CNY 121.98, so it is a statement about the company's own value range rather than a mark on today's price; it is still real capital committed rather than a press release.

Finally, the Hong Kong line is the cheap way in. At today's exchange rate of CNY 0.8559 to the Hong Kong dollar, the Hong Kong buyer pays CNY 89.53 per share for earnings the Shanghai buyer pays CNY 121.98 for — a 26.6% discount for identical economics. On the settled 727.1m share count the Hong Kong shares trade on about 13.3 times trailing earnings, 8.1 times enterprise value to earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation, and 9.9 times enterprise value to free cash flow. Nongfu Spring, the closest listed comparison for quality, trades today at roughly 24 times earnings and 15.7 times that same cash-profit measure on materially worse cash conversion.

For this to work, three things must hold. Revenue growth has to stabilise around the mid-teens rather than keep sliding — the 26 October 2026 third-quarter report is the first test. Gross margin has to hold above roughly 46% despite rising oil-linked bottle-resin costs. And the second-act products, chiefly the electrolyte drink, have to keep scaling against much larger entrants. If they do, a business earning 34% on equity with a quarter of its value in cash is worth meaningfully more than 13 times earnings.
bear_thesis:
The bear case is not that Eastroc is a bad business. It is that the recent earnings are flattered by something outside management's control, that the numbers the market is anchored to have not yet been cut, and that the only visible corporate bid was struck well above today's price.

Begin with the cheapness, because a large part of the advertised discount evaporates on inspection. Our own screening record shows a fair value of 392.98 and a 281% margin of safety. That figure extrapolates a 33%-a-year earnings growth rate that ended six months ago and, worse, compares a yuan-denominated output to a Hong Kong dollar price when the two currencies are 17% apart. It is arithmetically meaningless and must be discarded. The same record's 'earnings per share up only 2.0%' is the mirror-image error in the other direction — an artefact of the 3-for-10 bonus issue that took the share count from 520.0m to 676.0m, not an earnings stall. Once both errors are cleared and the denominator is settled at 727,076,759 shares, the stock trades on roughly 13 times trailing earnings and 3.3 times book value. That is a fair multiple for a mid-teens grower, not a distressed one — the bear case does not need the shares to be expensive, only to be priced for margins and volumes that may not arrive. Our own valuation stack agrees it is split: of five independent methods, two say the shares are overvalued (the earnings-power method by 84%, the owner-earnings method by 22%).

Second, the profit growth is being carried by a commodity windfall. Gross margin reached 49.2% in the June 2026 quarter against 45.7% a year earlier, a level the company has never sustained and which our screen flags as 1.35 standard deviations above the historical peak. Bottle resin is an oil derivative, and Brent crude rose 9.3% in the week to 4 September 2026 (USD 88.10 to USD 96.28) with the Strait of Hormuz shut. Strip the margin back to the 2025 level of 44.8% and roughly CNY 800m of annualised gross profit disappears — enough to turn 20% profit growth into low single digits on unchanged volumes. The one thing holding the earnings line up has just been handed a headwind.

Third, the published estimates are stale and have to come down. The consensus for the 2026 financial year, from 17 analysts, is revenue of CNY 28.09bn. The company delivered CNY 12.415bn in the first half. Getting to CNY 28.09bn requires roughly 55% second-half growth in a business that just printed 15.6%. Nobody would forecast that having seen the interim numbers, which means the estimates simply have not been revised. When they are, the stock will look more expensive on forward earnings than it does today, and downgrade cycles in Chinese consumer names have a way of running longer than the fundamentals warrant.

Fourth, the fall is a de-rating, not a dislocation. The shares came to Hong Kong in February 2026, ran to HKD 227.69, and have given it all back plus more. The Shanghai line fell almost as far, from CNY 241.06 to CNY 121.98, and Mixue — the other hot Chinese consumer listing of the same window — is down from HKD 465.80 to HKD 206.20. This is an entire cohort unwinding an initial-public-offering bubble. Buying the sixth month of a cohort de-rating on the grounds that the chart looks washed out has no edge in it, and a stock 2% off its 52-week low with no dated event to force a re-rate can spend a long time going nowhere.

Fifth, the one corporate bid in the file is not a valuation signal. The CNY 1.04bn repurchase that the bull case reads as management calling its own stock cheap was 7,122,551 A shares for CNY 1,038,719,867.57, an average of CNY 145.84, per the 2 September 2026 buyback progress announcement. That is roughly 20% above the CNY 121.98 the A shares fetch today. The company was buying, but it was buying higher; the programme says nothing about today's price being management's value point, and capital already spent above the current mark is not support beneath the shares.

What would confirm the bear case: third-quarter revenue growth on 26 October 2026 below roughly 12%, a gross margin back under 46%, or a fall in customer prepayments (CNY 5.13bn at 30 June) against the prior year, which would say distributors are destocking. Any of those and the earnings base itself, not just the multiple, is in question.
consensus_delta:
The usual question for a beaten-down value name is whether the market is pricing terminal decline into a business with stable earnings power. Here the answer is more interesting, and it cuts against us as much as for us: **the price has already worked out what the published estimates have not.**

The specific street assumption that is factually wrong is the 2026 revenue consensus. Seventeen analysts carry an average of CNY 28.09bn in a strikingly tight band of CNY 27.74bn to CNY 28.50bn. Eastroc delivered CNY 12.44bn of revenue in the first half of 2026. Reaching the consensus therefore requires second-half revenue of CNY 15.65bn against CNY 10.13bn a year earlier — growth of 54% — from a company that just grew 15.9%. No analyst who had read the interim report would publish that number. The estimates have simply not been refreshed since the results, and our own screening record's 'consensus forward earnings growth +12.4%' inherits the same stale base. The consensus earnings figure of CNY 5.64bn is less absurd but still demands 36% second-half profit growth against 20.7% delivered in the first half.

So where we disagree with the market is not that we are more bullish than the street — we are more bearish than the printed numbers, and roughly level with the price. The stock at HKD 104.60 already reflects a mid-teens grower; the estimates still describe a 35% grower. When those estimates are cut, the headlines will read as a downgrade cycle even though the price has known for months. That is the trap in this name: the obvious contrarian read — 'everyone hates it, the numbers are fine' — has the causality backwards.

There is one place where we genuinely differ from the tape, and it is narrower than the drawdown suggests. The market is treating the deceleration as a quality event. It is not. Profit grew faster than revenue (+20.7% against +15.9%), gross margin widened from 45.7% to 49.2% in the June quarter, return on equity is 33.7% after a large dilutive equity raise, distributors still pay in advance to the tune of CNY 5.13bn, and the cash conversion cycle is minus 20.6 days. Those are not the fingerprints of a franchise losing grip. A business with those characteristics growing profit at 20% is worth more than 16 times earnings — but 'more' here means roughly 19 times, not the 40-plus times the shares carried in the spring. The mispricing is real and it is about 17% wide. It is not the 281% our own screen advertised, and the gap between those two numbers is the whole reason this record exists.
forcing_function:
There is no hard date, no proxy window and no corporate event that contractually forces a re-rating here, and it would be dishonest to manufacture one. What exists is a sequence of scheduled checkpoints at which the market can change its mind.

**26 October 2026 — the third-quarter report** (date listed on TradingView's company page, retrieved 7 September 2026). This is the moment that matters most in the next six months. It answers the only question that decides this name: did revenue growth stabilise in the mid-teens, or did it keep sliding? And did gross margin hold above 46% as bottle-resin costs began to rise? A print showing 15%-plus revenue growth with the margin intact converts this from a watchlist name into a buy, because it would confirm that a 34%-return, net-cash franchise is being valued as a cyclical. **The customer prepayment line in that same report.** Contract liabilities were CNY 5.13bn at 30 June 2026. positioning_washout:
This is not a yield-driven shareholder base and there is no dividend cut in prospect, so the classic mechanical-liquidation setup does not apply. The dividend is roughly 2.1% of the price on the trailing payout of CNY 1.88 a share; note that two widely used data providers quote 5.5% and 6.0% for this name, both of which appear to annualise an older, higher payout against the new, much lower price. Working the other way, the company itself has been a buyer: roughly CNY 1.04bn of stock repurchased during the June 2026 quarter. That is the only large, price-insensitive bid visible in the file, and it is a real one.

The shares sit 2% above their 52-week low and 29% below their 200-day average, which is the profile of a market still finding sellers rather than one that has run out of them. A capitulation low, if it comes, would most likely be printed around the third-quarter report when the estimate cuts land.
moderator_conclusion:
**Buy it here.** The first pass called this a good business at a fair price and told the committee to wait for roughly HKD 90. That instruction rested on a denominator that has since been settled against the company's own filings, and with the correct one the same schedule produces a different answer.

The quality was never the argument. Eastroc earns a 33.7% return on equity, converts essentially all of its profit into cash, carries CNY 17.15bn of net cash — about a quarter of its market value on the settled count — and is paid in advance by its distributors to the tune of 23% of a year's revenue. Its cash conversion cycle is minus 20.6 days. Those are the marks of a genuine consumer franchise, and they are why the moat reads as narrow but real and stable rather than eroding: the margins are widening, not contracting, and no structural force this committee tracks threatens the terminal value of Chinese functional beverages.

The price is no longer the problem. On 727,076,759 shares outstanding the shares trade at about 13.3 times trailing earnings and 3.3 times book, roughly 10 times once net cash is stripped out. Base fair value is HKD 150 against a HKD 104.60 quote — a 30.3% discount, which clears this book's 20% entry-discount floor in the current GOLDILOCKS quadrant rather than missing it. Against an adverse case of HKD 82 the trade-off is 43% up for 22% down, a reward to risk of 2.01 where the first pass computed 0.46. There is still no structural floor: net cash is worth about HKD 27.5 a share and there is no deal, tender or fixed distribution to catch the price, so the downside remains bounded by the multiple.

Two of the three things that previously held the conviction at neutral survive; the third does not. The growth reset is real — 15.6% revenue growth in the first half of 2026 against 31.8% for 2025, confirmed on both listings — and the profit growth that survives is riding on a record 49.2% gross margin most plausibly caused by falling oil-linked input costs, with Brent up 9.3% in the week to 4 September 2026 and the Strait of Hormuz shut. That is the one place where the current regime reaches directly into this business, and it points against us; it is why the 18-month horizon and a mid-teens, not a mid-thirties, growth assumption are carried. The third holdback, the unresolved share count, is gone: 734,199,310 issued less 7,122,551 in treasury gives 727,076,759, tied to the interim distribution total and the Q2 weighted-average count. The record's own conservatism has been paid back rather than punished.

One bear-side fact travels with the correction and is worth stating plainly. The CNY 1.04bn buyback was executed at an average of CNY 145.84 an A share against CNY 121.98 today, so it is evidence of management's value range, not confirmation that today's price is their entry. It should not be read as a bid beneath the stock.

On the catalyst, we apply no penalty and no credit. The listing has happened and its re-rating has fully reversed; the buyback has happened; what remains is a soft catalyst with no fixed date and no contractual payout. In this book that is a description, not a mark against the name — but it is also why this is a conviction 4 and not higher: the discount is wide and the balance sheet is unarguable, yet nothing on the calendar forces the re-rating. The **26 October 2026 third-quarter report** remains the test that either accelerates it or breaks it: revenue growth holding at 15% or better with gross margin above 46% despite rising resin costs, and customer prepayments up year on year, and the case strengthens; a print below 12% growth or a margin under 46% and the earnings base, not just the multiple, is in question. Verdict held at B — the setup is a wide discount on a quality compounder without a dated forcing event, which is exactly what a B describes — with conviction lifted from 3 to 4 because the arithmetic that argued for waiting no longer does.
